findings.text: red-team lens, high: After zbuild_claim_acquire succeeds, the two early-failure return paths — _runner_enter_worktree failure and zbuild_run_branch_setup failure — call only zbuild_run_cap_release and return before the EXIT trap is installed (line 2940), so zbuild_claim_release is never called; the zbuild:claimed label stays on the issue permanently until removed by hand. (core/pipeline/runner.sh: "if ! _runner_enter_worktree "$state_dir" "$_runner_run_id" "$_wt_key"; then         zbuild_run_cap_release || true         return 1     fi"; happens when: A network outage or git error causes _runner_enter_worktree or zbuild_run_branch_setup to fail on a run that already acquired the claim; the process exits with no EXIT trap set, the label stays, and every subsequent run on the same issue is refused until an operator removes the label by hand.; fix: code)

red-team lens, medium: _ccgl_read_holder selects the last GitHub comment that contains the substring <!-- zbuild-run-status and extracts whatever the zbuild-holder field says; any user who can comment on the issue can craft a comment that becomes the most-recent match, injecting attacker-controlled content into the error message printed to the operator's terminal. (core/claim/claim.sh: "body="$(gh issue comment list "$issue" --json body \                 --jq '[.[] | select(.body | contains("<!-- zbuild-run-status")) | .body] | last' \                 2>/dev/null || true)""; happens when: An outside actor posts a comment on the issue whose body contains the string <!-- zbuild-run-status and a crafted <!-- zbuild-holder: EVIL --> line; the next refused run prints the crafted string verbatim (including terminal escape codes) in the error logged to the operator's shell.; fix: code)
